evidence.canonical_name: Read 2 Succeed (R2S) / Read To Succeed Asheville-Buncombe
evidence.summary: Read 2 Succeed is an Asheville/Buncombe County literacy nonprofit that recruits volunteer reading tutors who each commit to one K-5 student for a full school year, meeting twice weekly. The listed unit is a 3-session (6-hour) Zoom onboarding training required before tutors start, not the ongoing tutoring itself, but the org's own site describes an active tutor community (monthly 'Tutor Huddles' for coaching and connection, tutor recognition language) that persists beyond the one-off training.

evidence.note: All 3 listings are the same required training series (Jan 14/21/28, 6-8pm Zoom) for new volunteer reading tutors, not a recurring meetup in itself.

Description says tutors 'commit to one student for the full school year' and are 'trained, supported, and deeply connected to a network of people committed to literacy justice' - framing tutors as an ongoing corps, not one-time attendees.

Org's tutor page describes monthly 'Tutor Huddles' offering additional training, coaching, and 'the opportunity for tutors to connect and share ideas' - a standing recurring gathering for the tutor corps.
Page includes a 'R2S Reading Tutors Rock!' section and describes volunteers as 'the heart of our program,' language of membership/identity rather than a rotating commercial audience.
Search turned up a dedicated volunteer-opportunities page and a separate 'Apply to Volunteer' page, indicating an organized, ongoing volunteer program structure beyond a single training event.

evidence.canonical_name: BarCada (umbrella company of Ermantourage)
evidence.summary: BarCada is a multi-city commercial event company (umbrella of 'Ermantourage') running templated 'Dinner with Strangers' and 'Coffee with Strangers' event series in dozens of cities nationwide, not just Asheville. Each ticketed event ($23-$34) pairs two strangers one-on-one at a rotating restaurant or cafe based on a post-signup questionnaire about age, interests, and favorite foods; the 'Duos Edition' format is explicitly a one-time algorithmic pairing, not a returning membership.

evidence.note: 23 near-daily 'Dinner with Strangers' listings and 5 weekly 'Coffee with Strangers' listings, each at a different 'Restaurant/Cafe of the Day', priced $23-$34, described as 'meet a new friend one-on-one' with no mention of members, dues, or a group identity.
Tags include 'rotating-restaurant', 'structured networking', 'Icebreaker Prompts', 'Paired Seating' - language describing a facilitated matching service rather than a club with recurring attendees.

Eventbrite organizer page describes BarCada as 'the umbrella company of Ermantourage, an event series catering to the entertainment scene and the general public, which produces gatherings in many major cities.'

WebSearch turned up BarCada/Ermantourage running the identical 'Dinner with Strangers' and 'My 20's/30's in <city>' template in Arvada, Pomona, Warwick, Southlake TX, Albuquerque, Rocky Mount and other cities, confirming it is a nationwide commercial franchise format, not an Asheville-specific community.
No Asheville-specific Facebook group, Meetup, Discord, or 'about us' page for a local BarCada community was found; only the generic Eventbrite ticketing pages.

evidence.canonical_name: Foodies + New Friends (Ermantourage / ADDVentures)
evidence.summary: A ticketed ($31), monthly dinner meetup run by Ermantourage (by ADDVentures), a commercial event-production company operating the same 'Foodies + New Friends' format across 9+ cities nationwide (Hendersonville, Roseville, Fayetteville, Charlottesville, Los Angeles, etc.), each with rotating themed editions (Giving Back, Single Friends, 1-on-1). evidence.note: Ticketed at $31, organizer is 'Ermantourage NYC' (an out-of-town event company), and each listing's description is generic marketing copy identical across the series, not references to a specific returning membership.

The company's own site describes the format as strangers signing up individually for capped small-group dinners rotating across 9+ cities, explicitly a booking model rather than a fixed-membership group.

Ermantourage NYC runs many parallel event brands (Dinner with Entrepreneurs, Dinner with Strangers, Foodies + New Friends) across numerous cities, confirming it is a multi-city commercial event producer, not an Asheville-based community.

Search turned up near-identical 'Foodies + New Friends' listings for Hendersonville, Roseville, Summerville, Fayetteville, Charlottesville, and Los Angeles, all from the same organizer with the same $31 pricing pattern, reinforcing that Asheville is just one franchise stop rather than a standalone group.

Active Instagram presence (@steppinoutavl) alongside the dedicated steppinoutavl.org site, consistent with an ongoing community organization rather than a single instructor's class listing.

evidence.summary: A weekly house-hosted board game night at Hi-Wire Brewing's RAD Beer Garden taproom, part of the venue's regular weekly programming alongside 'Mug Mondays' and 'Trivia Tuesdays'. It's an open drop-in activity using the taproom's own game shelf plus BYO games, with no club name, membership, dues, or named organizer beyond the brewery itself.

evidence.note: Every one of the 29 weekly listings uses identical boilerplate: 'An open and casual game night featuring an assortment of board games available to play. Guests are welcome to bring their own games to share' - no membership or club language.
Tags are dominated by drop-in/walk-in language ('Drop In Play', 'Walk Ins Welcome', 'Casual Drop In', 'Open Play', 'Bring Your Own Game') rather than community/membership terms.

Hi-Wire's own site frames RAD Beer Garden as a taproom with regular weekly promotions (Mug Mondays, Trivia Tuesdays, etc.), consistent with Board Game Night being house programming rather than an independent club.

A separate 'Social Game Night' also held at this venue is run by the Meetup group 'Asheville 20's and 30's Social Group' and explicitly aimed at newcomers making new friends - confirms the venue hosts rotating-public game nights from outside organizers rather than having its own game-night club, and this Meetup organizer is distinct from the recurring MountainX-listed event being evaluated.

No Facebook group, Discord, newsletter, or 'members' page specific to a board game club at Hi-Wire RAD turned up in search; the venue's Facebook page (facebook.com/hiwirebrewingRAD) is the general brewery page, not a game-night community page.

evidence.canonical_name: Bluegrass Jam with Finkelstein 3 (Oklawaha Brewing Company)
evidence.summary: A weekly pickup bluegrass/old-time jam hosted by a house trio called Finkelstein 3 at Oklawaha Brewing Company in Hendersonville, running 6:30-8:30pm every Wednesday. Listings and tags describe it as a drop-in, all-skill-levels pickup circle ('bring your fiddle, banjo, guitar, mandolin, or just your ears') rather than a booked act, and it is catalogued by the Blue Ridge Music Trails project, which tends to document traditional jam sessions with a real community of returning pickers. No independent evidence was found of a distinct group identity, member roster, or dedicated group page separate from the brewery's own event listing.

evidence.note: Listings describe an instrumental pickup jam ('bring your fiddle, banjo, guitar, mandolin, or just your ears') at a brewery taproom, tagged Pickup Jam, Drop In Jam, Sit Ins Welcome, All Skill Levels rather than a ticketed show.
The brewery's own site lists 'Bluegrass Jam with Finkelstein 3' as a recurring Wednesday house event, with no further detail on participation or membership.

The jam is catalogued by the Blue Ridge Music Trails project (page itself returned a bot-check and no readable content), a regional heritage effort that specifically documents traditional old-time/bluegrass jam sessions as ongoing community gatherings, which is suggestive but not confirmed evidence of a returning core of players.
No dedicated Facebook group, Meetup page, or 'about the jam' page for the jam itself was found; only the brewery's own venue page and generic listing/review sites turned up.

evidence.summary: A weekly Sunday-evening open jam on the taproom stage at Pisgah Brewing Company in Black Mountain, run by the venue itself rather than a standing community. Each week's listing names a different rotating host or featured touring act (Spiro & Friends, Alex Bazemore, etc.) and explicitly invites 'any and all musicians' to sit in, with no membership, dues, sign-up form, or dedicated group page anywhere in the descriptions.

evidence.note: Description says 'Any and all musicians are welcome to come sit in' and 'The Jam is hosted by rotating special guests' with touring artists featured each week — classic drop-in open jam framing, not a member roster.

Across the five recurring listings the named host changes week to week (Spiro & Friends vs. unspecified 'rotating special guests'), and one unit is literally titled 'Sunday Jam with Spiro n Friends!' while others carry no host name at all, showing the jam is a venue-programmed slot, not one fixed act or crew.
No listing anywhere mentions members, a sign-up sheet, dues, a Facebook group, Meetup, Discord, or any organizing body other than Pisgah Brewing Company.

Etix ticketing shows the same 'Sunday Jam' slot also branded under a different named host (Alex Bazemore), confirming the series rotates its featured host rather than being run by one persistent group.

Web search for 'Spiro & Friends' turned up no dedicated band, page, or community for that name in Asheville — only that Spiro Nicolopoulos is one of several rotating hosts for this brewery-run jam night.

Pisgah Brewing's own site presents Sunday Jam as one of many recurring in-house show slots (alongside e.g. a Tuesday 'Bluegrass Open Jam'), i.e. venue programming rather than an independent club's regular meeting.

evidence.canonical_name: Free Mary Magdalene Meditation Circle (The Soul Institute / Adora Winquist)
evidence.summary: A free virtual monthly meditation webinar hosted solo by Adora Winquist of The Soul Institute, cross-posted to Eventbrite under near-identical city-tagged listings (AVL, New York, St. Louis, and many other cities) for local SEO/ad targeting. All three listings share the exact same location field 'Virtual, Asheville, NC' and the identical first-person-singular description ('I invite you to meditate with me...'), indicating one host running one recurring session, not distinct local communities. It functions as a lead-generation funnel into Adora's paid retreats and membership, not a returning-member circle.

evidence.note: All three 'city' variants (AVL, New York, St. Louis) list the identical location 'Virtual, Asheville, NC' and word-for-word identical first-person description 'I invite you to meditate with me...', showing one host running one session under multiple city-targeted slugs.

No membership language anywhere in the descriptions or tags — no 'our group', 'members', dues, or named regulars; tags are generic wellness/marketing terms (Healing Focus, Self Mastery, Personal Transformation).
The Soul Institute is Adora Winquist's personal wisdom-school brand (Asheville-based); she runs paid retreats, a 'Pathway Membership', and products, with the free circle as an entry funnel.

site:eventbrite.com search shows the same 'Free Mary Magdalene Meditation Circle' listing replicated for many other cities (LA, Nashville, Miami, San Diego, Charleston, Boston, San Francisco), all the same 1st-Tuesday 7-7:40pm EST session, confirming a city-tagged ad-targeting pattern rather than distinct communities.

A Meetup group under The Soul Institute's name was found referenced but its page now 404s, suggesting any attempt at a persistent membership platform was abandoned; social presence (Instagram @adorawinquist, Facebook) is tied to Adora personally, not a 'Mary Magdalene Circle' community page.

evidence.summary: "Next Gen" is named as the host of "Art After Dark," a monthly First-Friday late-night social/art mixer at the YMI Cultural Center in Asheville, described as celebrating Black art and Black social life. Only two listings exist (June and July 2026), both free and ticketed generically through Eventbrite under organizer "YMI Cultural Center" rather than a "Next Gen" organizer account, and no independent website, Facebook group, Meetup, or Instagram presence for a group called "Next Gen" could be found tied to YMI.

evidence.note: June listing: 'Join us for our new First Friday initiative that celebrates Black Art and Black Social Life' — framed as a new recurring series, not an established club, with no membership/dues/sign-up language.
July listing: 'Hosted by Next Gen, this exciting evening brings together all things community' — names Next Gen as host but gives no bio, links, or description of who Next Gen's members are.

Both events list the organizer as 'YMI Cultural Center,' not 'Next Gen,' and tags include 'Next Gen Creatives,' 'Community Mixer,' 'Social Mixer,' and 'LGBTQ+' — consistent with either a young-adults affinity group or simply a branded nightlife program name.
YMI Cultural Center's own site lists its programs (Goombay, Ujima Health & Wellness, tours, gallery, event rentals) with no mention of 'Next Gen' or 'Art After Dark' anywhere.
Rendered Eventbrite page has no organizer bio, social links, or membership info beyond the bare event details; no independent Facebook group, Meetup, or Instagram for 'Next Gen' turned up.
